dedupe_keys.name: four european city airport pairs multimodal accessibility analysis

description: University of Parma researchers compared four pairs of small or remote European airports and their surrounding cities. The application joins airport, municipality, air-carrier and route information with roadway and coastal-shipping links, collected mainly in 2018–2019 from public portals, owners and project meetings. The Data in Brief article documents GIS network analysis and database calculations that yield airport access, proximity and origin–destination views. Its article is open under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, while the separate supplemental archive has no independently verified reuse licence. The study covers four selected airport pairs in the pre-pandemic period; it is not a current network model for all European airports. Data-source differences, unknown supplement contents and changed travel patterns are limitations. The achieved result is a structured comparison of multimodal links and planning measures, not evidence that an airport intervention was implemented. A reviewer-assessed use is testing how regional airport links or access options change under scenarios. G2-0621 is the related supplemental data draft; no executable calculation package or direct GIS import was verified. No archive was downloaded.
name: Four European city-airport pairs multimodal accessibility analysis
notes: G2-0625. Case-study record for the documented application. Distinct from the linked data-deposit draft; publication does not prove an infrastructure intervention was implemented.
outcomes: The researchers assembled four pairs of small or remote European airports and calculated air-route and land or coastal access relationships, including origin–destination and proximity measures for city-airport planning. The article does not demonstrate a policy change or post-2019 operational benefit.
